speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the nature of your altered mental status and fever. Have you experienced any recent head trauma, seizures, or severe headache? Also, have you been traveling or exposed to anyone with similar symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history is helpful; given your tics and haloperidol use, could you clarify if the altered mental status involves confusion, hallucinations, or excessive sedation, and have you noticed any muscle rigidity or tremors? Additionally, please tell me if you have experienced any recent changes in sleep patterns or appetite.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) caused by Haloperidol.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, Creatine Kinase (CK), and Urinalysis.
REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage.
